sense.text:
“Is not this the fast that I have chosen?” This is the fast of all fasts, the one the Most High ordained on the Day of Atonement for the forgiveness of all the sins we commit in the body, willingly and unwillingly, so that we can start all over with a clean slate. We keep voluntary fasts too, asking the Most High in prayer and supplication to forgive us, but this is the fast. Imagine if we did not have that day: all those sins would weigh us down and plague us. That is why he is a merciful God, a forgiving God. And still some brothers would not keep it, because they had to work or they got hungry. That makes no sense.

The fast is “to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens”. Many of our people are plagued in their minds by the heavy burdens of the sins they have committed through the years, and the fast undoes them. It is “to let the oppressed go free”, spiritually and physically, “and that ye break every yoke”: every spiritual yoke, every physical yoke, and the mental yokes we put on our own minds when we think the Most High will not forgive us.

It does not matter if in the world you were a punk, a man dealing with other men, a homosexual; a sister who was dealing with other women; into drugs, fornication, pornography, soliciting prostitutes. All these things can be forgiven. We cannot let those mental yokes plague us.

precepts.why:
“Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins”. Through this man, Jesus Christ, the forgiveness of sins is preached to the Israelites. We serve a merciful God who forgives us of our sins. We do not have to continue in them, and we do not have to let them weigh us down.

“And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.” If you say you believe you are an Israelite, and that Jesus Christ, the black Messiah, died for our sins, you are justified. Under the law of sacrifice we could not be justified, because blood had to be spilled. But Christ died once and for all for our sins so that we may be forgiven.

That is why it is a beautiful thing that the Most High set up the Day of Atonement for us to keep, with fasting. It is how the heavy burdens of Isaiah 58:6 are undone and the yokes broken.

sense.text:
“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor”. The spirit of the Lord was on Jesus Christ, and now it is on us, because Christ is not physically here with us anymore but is with us in spirit: we are the body of Christ. The poor are not everybody. This is not the Christian church and not Christianity; the Bible is the book for the Israelites, by the Israelites, and Christ was talking to the Israelites. The poor is Israel. The gospel is the good news, and the good news is not for all nations; that is a damn lie.

“He hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted”: the broken in spirit, the broken in mind. A lot of our people are plagued in the mind by the sins that weigh them down. The brokenhearted is Israel.

“To preach deliverance to the captives”: examine history and we are the captives, the ones taken into captivity and brought on slave ships, as Deuteronomy 28 documents. That history did not happen to anyone but the so-called blacks, Latinos and Native Americans, the captive Israelites. Even to this day, look at who makes up the majority of the prison population: it is us. We go to jail in record numbers, we are set up for failure with the school to prison pipeline, because they do not want to see us succeed. And as long as we keep breaking God’s commandments, this is what will happen to us. Everybody is not in captivity; we are.

“And recovering of sight to the blind”: the blind is Israel. “To set at liberty them that are bruised”: the yokes leave a scar, a bruise, a mark, and we are the ones who need healing from that.

“To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.” That is what we have to do. Once we heal ourselves, our minds, our bodies, our spirits, we preach the acceptable year of the Lord: the redeeming of the Israelites and the second coming of the black Messiah, Jesus Christ.

So brothers, take the Day of Atonement very seriously; take fasting and prayer very seriously. We do not have a lot of time. We do not have time to wallow in our sins, our depression, our distress. We have a nation that needs healing and help, and we have to get ourselves together so that we can go out and help those who are in distress and depression, just like we were.

precepts.why:
“That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.” The poor of whom? Of his people. “His” is possessive. It is not talking about all people; it says his people.

So the poor that Jesus Christ preached the gospel to in Luke 4:18 are the Israelites, the poor of Israel. This is not the Christian church and the gospel is not for everybody.

The good news is “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people”. The Lord God of Israel, and his people, Israel. You cannot get all nations out of that.

That is the gospel preached to the poor in Luke 4:18, and it is good news to us because we are the ones the curses are upon. Read Deuteronomy 28, verses 15 to 68: we fit the curses. So who needs salvation, grace and mercy? Us, the so-called blacks, Latinos and Native Americans, who are the Israelites.

“Praise ye the Lord: for it is good to sing praises unto our God; for it is pleasant; and praise is comely.”

“The Lord doth build up Jerusalem: he gathereth together the outcasts of Israel.” It is always talking about Israel, never about all nations: the outcasts of Israel are the Israelites scattered to the four corners of the earth.

“He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.” He heals the broken in spirit: the same brokenhearted Christ was sent to heal in Luke 4:18. Remember the yokes: a physical yoke on the arms or the neck, shackles on the feet, cut and wound and leave a scar. We have had those. That is what happened to our people: mental scars, spiritual scars and physical scars from slavery and trauma. So we as a nation need healing, and we have to preach this gospel to our people so that they may be healed and get the help they cry out for.

“Recovering of sight to the blind” in Luke 4:18 is shown here. “We grope for the wall like the blind”: picture a blind man touching the wall, trying to get his footing, trying to find himself. “We grope as if we had no eyes”: that is Israel searching. We go to Christianity searching, to Islam searching, into the world searching, for an identity and for help.

“We stumble at noonday as in the night”. At noonday the sun is most high and it is bright outside, and still we stumble, as if it were night, because we are blind: blind to the truth, blind to our true nationality, blind to the true identity of Christ, the black Messiah, a black man who died for our sins and our sins only. We do not know who we are.

“We are in desolate places as dead men.” The desolate places are where the truth is not taught: Christianity, the church system here in Babylon, preaching a white Jesus, a white Christ, a white God, and teaching that the Jewish people are God’s chosen people. These are all lies. That is why bishops, deacons, captains, officers and soldiers go to the four corners of the earth, to the desolate places, looking for the blind Israelites, the lost Israelites who need healing and help.

The Bible calls us dead men when we wander out of this truth: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.” That is the Israelite man who wanders out of the way of understanding.

That is why Isaiah 59:10 says we are “in desolate places as dead men.” When we wander from this understanding of who we are, we are as dead men. The only thing that brings us to life is God’s scriptures and God’s laws; without them we are nothing. The blind that Christ gives sight to in Luke 4:18 are these dead men of Israel.

sense.text:
You have to want to come out of the depressed spirit, and it starts with having pride in yourself, even in something that seems small like your name. In the world we took pride in our last names. But our name is above all names. “Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel”: our forefather’s name was changed from Jacob to Israel. That is who we descend from, our lineage, our bloodline: great men, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. We come from Christ, and we are the body of Christ. That has to wake our spirit up and move us.

“For as a prince hast thou power with God”. The Most High is calling us a prince. When you call yourself Israel, you are saying you are a prince with power with God. That is what your name means. Take pride in it; it should motivate you to come out of that stupor, that woe is me mentality, that depressed and distressed spirit. Go into the scriptures and see yourself in these words.

We cannot stay wallowing in our sins and our depression; we are greater than that. Do not let Satan come over you and separate you from the body, because that is what he wants. As long as he has you by yourself, you are vulnerable. Stay within the pack: the wolf pack, the lion’s pride.

precepts.why:
The Most High told us to go to the ants. The ants were seen picking up a whole lizard and carrying it home: it took them a long time, but they did it through teamwork and unity. One ant is weak, and you could crush it with your thumb, but together they are strong, and so are we. How much greater are we than these ants? Alone you will not move anything; together we can move mountains and do great works.

“Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise”. Thou lazy person, slothful. A lot of us get lazy, too comfortable in our captivity, wanting only to go home and be on our phones, on TikTok and Instagram all day. Consider her ways: how they move in unity, the strength in numbers. That is how we become wise. You are not going to do this by yourself, and you do not have to be by yourself. There is help.

The ant has “no guide, overseer, or ruler”, yet she “Provideth her meat in the summer, and gathereth her food in the harvest.” We have guides and overseers: bishops, deacons, captains, officers. If the ant, a small thing in our eyes, and how much smaller in the Most High’s eyes, is wise enough to work in unity, so must we be. Do not stray from the pack.

sense.text:
“For as he thinketh in his heart, so is he”. As you think of yourself in your heart, that is what you are going to be. If you think of yourself as nothing, you will always be nothing. It starts up here, in how you think of yourself, and that is why we have to take pride in who we are. We are the Israelites; we read over and over how the Most High delivers us and shows us mercy, grace and forgiveness.

You think you are nothing, you will always be nothing; you have to come to a change. That is why Samuel was sent to Saul. Saul did not want to be king and thought little of himself, but the Most High anointed him to be the first king over Israel, and Samuel had to be sent to him. That is why we are sent to our people: to preach the day of the Lord, the second coming of Jesus Christ.

We have to see ourselves in the scriptures, the greatness we come from and what the Most High wants for us. You have to want it for yourself; no one can give it to you. You have to work for it, drive yourself, motivate yourself, whether that is abstaining from fleshly lust and social media, fasting and praying, or coming around the body on the high holy days and the Sabbath. We are the first fruits, and we have to build ourselves up.

precepts.why:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.” Do you believe that? This is how a wise master builder moves the people out of a depressed, weak spirit into the joyful spirit of the Most High’s high holy days: he has them say it after him until they believe it, “above all people”.

That is our lot. When you say you are an Israelite, that is what you are saying: you are above all people that are upon the face of the earth. There is no nation above the Israelites. We have to keep that in our minds and believe it, because as a man thinketh in his heart, so is he.

That is why we go into the scriptures, for direction and motivation, and that is how we have to motivate our people. If you say you are Israel, you are here for a reason and a purpose: to get better so that you can go out and teach your people, so that they can have the same chance to repent and be redeemed.

sense.text: “Give not over thy mind to heaviness”. Heaviness is depression and distress. “And afflict not thyself in thine own counsel”: that is you separating yourself, straying from the pack, from the body, from the pride. You have to stay within the congregation, because that is where the help is and where you are strongest. When we are together: go to the ant, thou sluggard, and be wise. Giving your mind to heaviness and afflicting yourself in your own counsel will lead to depression, stress and distress.

“The gladness of the heart is the life of man”. That is why we go into the scriptures, to Deuteronomy 7:6, Genesis 32:28, Luke 1:68: they are supposed to bring us gladness and joy. Why do you think we have so many high holy days? Because we come from trauma and depression, and the Most High is bringing us out of it. The joy of the Lord is your strength, so we have to gather ourselves together. “And the joyfulness of a man prolongeth his days”: joyfulness prolongs our days.

“Love thine own soul”. You have to love yourself; no one is going to love you more than you love yourself. “And comfort thy heart”: comfort your mind. The things you did in the past, put them behind you and do not dwell on them. “Remove sorrow far from thee: for sorrow hath killed many”. Stress breaks your body down and brings affliction: heart failure, organ failure, cancer, diseases come from stress and sorrow.

“And there is no profit therein.” There is no profit in always being down, always depressed, separating yourself. You have to be joyful and glad, and you do that by coming around the body. When brothers are together we build, we go over scriptures, we laugh, we joke, we console one another. After the high holy days, after camp and powerful teaching, you are forced up at five in the morning in the dark to go work for Esau or the other nations, and wait two weeks to get paid for your labor for the enemy. That is depressing. You come out of it by coming around the body and building yourselves up in your most holy faith.

precepts.why:
“A merry heart doeth good like a medicine”. A merry mind does good like a medicine. Being joyful and glad, especially on the Most High’s high holy days, is medicine to your mind and your spirit. So when you come in here, shake the depressed spirit off and leave it at the door. You may be stressed out, with bills and things going on in your personal life, but once you come through these doors you forget them, even if for a little moment.

“But a broken spirit drieth the bones.” A broken spirit, a broken mind, a broken brother or sister: it dries up your bones and causes sickness. So we have to come out of that thing. And you are not alone: we have congregations throughout the face of the earth. Israel is growing, and we are not small anymore.

This is the gladness of the heart that Ecclesiasticus 30:22 calls the life of man.

“For of heaviness cometh death”. Heaviness is depression and distress, and it can cause you to die: internal organ failure, and thoughts of suicide. Brothers have thoughts of suicide because they let the depression get to them.

“And the heaviness of the heart breaketh strength.” It makes you weak. It makes you not want to eat, not want to congregate, not want to come around the brothers anymore. That is why Ecclesiasticus 30:21 says, give not over thy mind to heaviness. So how do we get our strength, our healing, our help?

This was spoken on a high holy day, and we just kept the feast of tabernacles. “Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet”: at tabernacles we were eating and drinking as a body, a congregation, around the bishops and deacons, the captains and officers, the tribes set up, everywhere shalom. It was healing and nurturing to the spirit: the unity, the healing of a nation. Tents open and nothing lost, no fights, no arguments, all joy: a glimpse of what the future will look like for us.

“And send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared”: single brothers and single sisters; nobody went hungry at tabernacles. There was a spirit of giving and sharing: what is mine is yours. “For this day is holy unto our Lord”: the feast day is holy unto the Lord.

“Neither be ye sorry”. We have to stop feeling sorry for ourselves. The day of the Lord is a beautiful thing, and being an Israelite while we see the Most High moving and the nations at war, all for the deliverance of the nation of Israel, is a beautiful thing. “For the joy of the Lord is your strength.” It brings joy to the Most High’s heart when we come together, and that is our strength. Even when you are distressed and depressed, shake it off, because it can make you sick. That is the gladness and joyfulness of Ecclesiasticus 30:22 that prolongs our days.

sense.text:
Some of the causes of depression in brothers and sisters are fornication, porn and masturbation, and it has to be spoken of, because twelve, thirteen, fourteen year olds deal with it, and adults deal with it, especially the single brothers and sisters. If you do not talk about it, you cannot fix it. The number one sufferers of promiscuity are the children: teenage pregnancies, abortions, broken homes, unwanted children, syphilis, gonorrhea, herpes. Esau in his wicked mind says boyfriend and girlfriend is okay, and society promotes promiscuity, gay sex, homosexuality and lesbianism. So we have to preach marriage, between a man and a woman. It does not get preached enough.

“Marriage is honourable in all”. It is an honor in the eyes of the Most High, a beautiful thing to see a husband and wife dwell together in unity. “And the bed undefiled”: what a man does with his wife in the bed chamber is undefiled, as long as you do not bring in another person, a device or an animal. Those things are fornication in the eyes of the Most High, lasciviousness, wickedness.

“But whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.” Men sleeping with multiple women and calling them their wives: the scripture calls that whoremongering. You are a whoremonger, not a husband; you cannot afford more than one wife, and that is just you feeding your sexual lust. A man who steps out of his marriage is an adulterer, and a woman who steps out of hers is an adulteress. God will judge you for those wicked acts.

So we have to promote the sanctity of marriage. It is one of our biggest weapons: with marriage comes stability for the children, economics that stay strong because they are passed down within our own people, less disease, and righteous children. Many in our communities grow up without a father because the mother was promiscuous or a teen mom. The boy raised without a father grows up an emotional thug in the streets, and the streets are filled with young men and women as a result of broken homes. We have to be the righteous example and stop that vicious cycle, and it starts with promoting marriage.

Social media and the phone were set up by Esau to destroy the minds of our people and our youth. Porn is easy access now; kids can be looking at it on their phones right in front of you. Put a lock on your phone, get a flip phone, delete the apps that are destroying you. Mothers and sisters with children, check their phones: you bought that phone, and there is no privacy in Israel. Do not think it is all good just because they wear fringes and their heads are wrapped. Do not sleep.

“Be sober”: be clear minded. “Be vigilant”: always looking out for the evil, the traps, the wiles. “Because your adversary the devil”: devil means adversary, and our adversary is Esau, the other nations, but specifically Esau, who runs the system of Babylon.

“As a roaring lion”: when a lion roars it is loud. In the zoo you often do not hear it, because the lion in captivity is depressed, waiting for the sons of God to wake up and save them out of captivity. “Walketh about”: scheming, plotting. “Seeking whom he may devour”: he devours us through the wiles of the devil, the devices of Satan: the cell phone, the internet, social media.

Porn will put a spirit on you. As Bishop likes to say, porn is gay, and that is what you have to tell yourself: you are looking at another man having sex with a woman, looking at a man’s private, when you should not look on the nakedness of anyone who is not your wife. That spirit jumps on you, you start thinking homosexual acts, and when you do not have access to a woman you go to a man. Then come worse things like NAMBLA, because regular sex does not do it for you anymore; you normalize it and are desensitized to it. That is the wiles of the devil. Satan is not giving up, so we cannot give up, cannot sleep; we have to be on guard at all times.

precepts.why:
Looking at porn sites opens a gate you will not be able to close if you do not control it. “When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest, and findeth none.” You were dealing with one spirit, and it left, looking for a place.

“Then he saith, I will return into my house from whence I came out”. That is why we have to remain vigilant: Satan is not sleeping; he is walking around waiting to come back and knock on your door again. “And when he is come, he findeth it empty, swept, and garnished.” You are not doing the work, not studying, not communicating: that is an empty, garnished place for Satan to come in.

“Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more wicked”. The straight porn you used to watch turns into man and man, woman and woman, a dog and a woman, pedophilia. You were dealing with one spirit; now you have invited all those unclean spirits into your life once you opened the gate of porn. Young brothers especially, single brothers who are dealing with it heavier: control it. That is how the devil walks about seeking whom he may devour.

sense.text:
Pornography eliminates the need for courage: you do not need game to talk to a woman when you can go to a website. Brothers come out socially awkward, unable to talk to a real woman, ready for AI sex dolls, sitting on their mama’s couch. It destroys your happiness; a chronic porn watcher is like a crackhead chasing the first high he will never get back. And the brother who wants to be married will not be able to satisfy his wife. That is where the depression and distress come in, because you were not patient enough to wait and prove a sister. Pornography is a device of Amalek, the impostor, to keep us in sin so he can stay on top.

“Flee fornication.” “Every sin that a man doeth is without the body”: when you are in fornication you are doing it outside of the body; you have chosen to separate yourself, because that is not supposed to go on in here. “But he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body.” You sin against yourself, and it brings you diseases and sometimes death, because you are outside the realm of what God ordained for us.

“What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you”. Our bodies are temples of the Holy Ghost, and the Holy Ghost is the laws; it is supposed to dwell in your temple, in your body. When you are in fornication you are defiling that temple, harming and destroying yourself. “Which ye have of God”: God gave us this body for the spirit to dwell in. “And ye are not your own”: we are not our own.

“For ye are bought with a price”: the blood of Christ. “Therefore glorify God in your body”: in the works you do and the offices you are responsible for. Flee fornication and flee sin, because when you do them you defile and destroy your temple. “And in your spirit, which are God’s”: they belong to God.

“For this is the will of God, even your sanctification”: your holiness, your cleansing. Evil cannot dwell in a defiled temple; the Holy Spirit will flee fornication. “That ye should abstain from fornication”.

To abstain is to choose not to do or have something; to refrain deliberately, and often with an effort of self-denial, from an action or practice. You have to be deliberate: delete the apps from your phone and the porn sites from your computer, put a lock on it, have a brother create a password so you cannot get in, and use it only for the Lord’s work. It is easy access and free now, so be deliberate. It will not happen on its own and you will not suddenly be super strong; you have to put effort into self-denial of the fleshly lusts and self-gratifications like pornography and masturbation. Pornography leads to masturbation; nobody watches porn for the cinematography. The action is masturbating; the practice is pornography and prostitution, buying women, going on OnlyFans.

“That every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour”. You have to know how to possess the vessel God gave you, in holiness and honor. It was not given to you for self-gratification, masturbation, pornography and fornication; it was given for a purpose: to go and teach the people, to heal the broken people, to preach deliverance. If you are into pornography, masturbation, prostitution or soliciting, you cannot do the work. You will be a hypocrite, you will feel guilty, and you will start separating yourself: I’m not feeling well, I can’t make it to camp. We have to let the Holy Spirit dwell in us, not the demonic entities pornography brings.

“Not in the lust of concupiscence”. Concupiscence is strong desire, especially sexual desire: the burning desire you get when you want to watch porn and gratify yourself. “Even as the Gentiles which know not God”: the other nations that do not know God. We cannot be like them. You dishonor the body God gave you when you deal in pornography, fornication and masturbation. These are the scriptures we have to read to bring us out of the abyss, out of the depressed spirit and the evil concupiscence that comes over us when we are alone, without the unity and strength of the body.

“As we also have forewarned you and testified.” This is a forewarning and a testimony: stop dealing in pornography, fornication and masturbation. It only leads to depression and to worse sins; there are levels to it. A homosexual spirit, a lesbian spirit, bestiality, looking at children as sexual objects: all these things come when you deal in pornography.

precepts.why:
“Now the works of the flesh are manifest”. We are vessels where the Holy Spirit is supposed to dwell and sanctify us, but these are the works of the flesh, what we are dealing with in pornography and fornication. “Adultery, fornication, uncleanness”: you are no longer holy or sanctified. “Lasciviousness”: looking at another man’s wife or another woman’s husband, looking at a man the way you look at a woman, looking at a child: wicked, evil sexual desires.

“Hatred”: you start hating your brother because you cannot get yourself right, hating what he has and how he got his family in order. “Murders”: the woman you met on the internet is only there because you paid her, and she laughs at you because you are sexually inadequate and socially awkward; then a murderous spirit comes on you and you kill her because she does not want you like you want her. “Drunkenness”: you have to get drunk to talk to a woman. “Revellings”: you go to the party where everybody is promiscuous because it is easy.

“They which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.” We all want the kingdom of God, but if we deal in the lust of the flesh we will not inherit it. So before you go to that porn site, before you go on OnlyFans, before you go where the prostitutes are, consider this. That is why the will of God is that we abstain from fornication.

There is an out. You have time to be watching porn because you do not do enough in the body or for yourself: get busy in the work, go to the gym, get a real job. Too much idle time brings sin; idleness is Satan’s playground.

“There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able”. The Lord will give you that out if you are sincere and trying to get your life right. It may be a brother calling you just when you are about to do that evil: the Lord will send somebody your way to get you out of it.

“But will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” All brothers burn; that burn is real for the single brother. But the Lord will provide an out so that you do not give in to the temptation, because he is merciful and will help you if you are sincere. That is how you can abstain from fornication.

The key is to be sincere and confess. A lot of us deal with pride and are ashamed of confessing, but we are all sick in here, and we all come to be healed by the word of the Lord and helped by our leadership.

“Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed.” If you confess that you are dealing with it, we are able to pray for that iniquity or impurity; we cannot pray for it if we do not know. Then you begin to heal and move away from the porn and the fornication.

“The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.” The prayer of our leadership, and of the brothers and sisters, will heal you up. There is power behind it, so do not minimize it.

sense.text:
“Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims”: that is what we are here in Babylon. We want our kingdom and our homeland, Israel, Jerusalem. “Abstain from fleshly lusts”: abstain, refrain, be deliberate in your efforts. The lust of the flesh is the self-gratification, the instant gratification, the first hit of crack we look for in pornography and masturbation.

“Which war against the soul”. It is a war between the flesh and the spirit, and it is up to you to decide who wins. You thought it was a game; it is a war, so be mindful of what you signed up for. Esau is war ready; he was made for war. What are you made for? Build yourself up, strengthen your mind, your spirit and your body. Be deliberate and put forth effort, because it will not happen on its own.

“And that the faces of them which have used abstinence”: those who abstained, refrained, were deliberate in their efforts, and did not deal in pornography, lust, lasciviousness, fornication and evil concupiscence, “shall shine above the stars”. That is literal and spiritual. Brothers who deal in pornography get a dullness about them: they do not study like they used to, there is a different countenance on them, their spirit is not right, and unless they confess their fault, Satan has them. But fill your vessel with the Holy Spirit, the laws, do the work of the Most High, and you will shine with a godlike confidence and a glow; brothers will want to be around you and you will have a joyful spirit. If you do not abstain, that light starts to dim.

“Whereas our faces shall be blacker than darkness”: that is what happens if we do not abstain.

Abstain, abstinence, be deliberate: we look up these words because similar, easier words make it plain what God wants for us. Many of us dealt with pornography and masturbation; we all did, and you have to confess it now. Being deliberate means this: make it one week without watching porn, then two weeks, then a month, then two and three months. Once you see you really do not need it, you start thinking clearer.

“For while we lived and committed iniquity, we considered not that we should begin to suffer for it after death.” When you were watching porn, gratifying yourself and chasing the lust of the flesh, you did not consider that there is a price to pay for that sin. After death is the second death, when Christ returns to destroy the nations and the wicked Israelites who chose to remain in sin: we are already dead without these laws, and after death we will continue to suffer in hell.

“This is the condition of the battle, which man that is born upon the earth shall fight”. We are in a battle, a war between the flesh and the spirit, and you decide who wins. Walk in the spirit, walk in the light, and do not be overcome by sin. Otherwise depression sets in: I’m not worthy, I don’t think I’m an Israelite, moping and wallowing in your sins, and that spirit jumps on everyone else. Think of your brothers and sisters and the condition of our people. God chose you out of millions of our people to be a vessel for good, and you destroy that vessel with pornography, fornication and masturbation.

precepts.why:
What is the darkness of 2 Esdras 7:55? “Arise, shine; for thy light is come”: the Lord’s Christ is come, “and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.” That is what we have to see in you, brothers: the glory of the Lord, not that blackness and darkness.

“For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth”: the earth is covered with pornography, lasciviousness, all kinds of sin and evil. “And gross darkness the people”: the earth is in darkness, but our people are in gross darkness, total darkness, no light. Esau has us thinking we are nothing, good for nothing, to be raised in the ghetto and the projects. Not knowing who you are, not knowing that God and Christ look like you, not knowing what to do to come out of the conditions your people are in, killing your brother who looks just like you, stealing from your own people: that is gross darkness, sin covering our people.

“But the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.” That is why we march and go into the highways and hedges and the corners: not for vain glory, but because God commands us to, so that people see the light and there is no longer gross darkness. We light up the world with God’s laws and commandments, boots on the ground, as the example and guiding light. We are the leaders, and we have to see ourselves as such. Those who abstain shine; those in sin are in darkness.

The condition of the battle is a choice. “By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter”. Moses was a prince in Egypt, considered the son of Pharaoh’s daughter, “Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season”.

The Most High understands that sin is pleasurable; if it were not, we would not be chasing it. But we have to choose affliction with our people over the pleasure of sin. Put yourself in the scriptures and use them to come out of the condition you are in.

“For a season” means it comes to an end. It does not last forever, and after that season is over comes death. That is the battle every man born on the earth must fight.

sense.text:
Another reason brothers and sisters get depressed is a bad marital breakup: your wife left you, your husband left you. Some brothers come in all depressed, tears in their eyes, voice cracking, looking for us to rub their back and tell them they can take her back. You have to snap out of it. Once that woman sleeps with another man, it is a wrap: she caught a body on you, and she is not yours. Brothers will take that defiled woman back because they are weak and depressed and think there is no one else. That is why we have the simp intervention: left to your own thoughts you will say, we were good together, we can fix it. We push you through that door. Accept it: she is not your woman, she is a community broad. Let it out, come to your brothers for help, and do not be afraid to start all over.

“If a man put away his wife, and she go from him, and become another man’s, shall he return unto her again?” That is a rhetorical question, and the answer is no. “Shall not that land be greatly polluted?” That woman is greatly polluted. When you sleep with her, you sleep with every man she laid with, and every woman that man laid with, on and on: infinite bodies. And if you do take her back, you will think about that other man, and it will put a murderous spirit on you; no amount of beating will take those spirits out of her. There is nothing there but death, destruction and more depression.

“But thou hast played the harlot with many lovers; yet return again to me”. Here the Most High is talking about us as a nation: we played the harlot with many lovers in the world, Christianity, Islam. But we cannot do what the Most High has done with us. If the woman you chose lays with another man, it is over and you cannot take her back. That is fornication and wickedness.

precepts.why:
“Know ye not that your bodies are the members of Christ?” Our bodies are the members, the vessels, the temple of Christ. “Shall I then take the members of Christ, and make them the members of an harlot? God forbid.” You cannot take God’s member and put it with a harlot. It does not mix.

“Know ye not that he which is joined to an harlot is one body? for two, saith he, shall be one flesh.” He that is joined to an harlot is one body with her, and you are a whoremonger. You do not want to be counted a whoremonger.

So you cannot take that woman back of Jeremiah 3:1, no matter how badly you want her, no matter the memories or the children you had with her. Put that woman away. Once another man went in her and she caught that body, it is not the same.

“I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him, until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness.” That is what you have to tell yourself.

“Then she that is mine enemy shall see it”: the wife who played the harlot and laid with another man is your enemy. She hates you and does not love you. When she sees you in that new, righteous light with a new, righteous family, rebuilt because you showed mental and spiritual fortitude and left her, “shame shall cover her”, because she lost the good man, the fine gold who could deliver her from captivity and was guiding her. She chose the rod, death and destruction.

“Which said unto me, Where is the Lord thy God?”: she was an unbelieving spouse. “Mine eyes shall behold her: now shall she be trodden down as the mire of the streets.” That mud, that filth, is how you have to look at the woman who played the harlot, disrespected you and showed you hatred. That is why the man of Jeremiah 3:1 shall not return unto her again.

sense.text:
For the brother whose wife left him, who cannot see his kids, there is Mike Tyson: in pain, not caring if he lives or dies, wanting to strip his opponents of their health. That warrior spirit has to wake up in you. Turn into a spiritual Mike Tyson and go out and blaze in this truth; take the wickedness that woman did and take it out on the nation in teaching the word.

“Iron sharpeneth iron”. Iron Mike Tyson: we turn brothers into spiritual Mike Tysons in here, the young warrior knocking dudes out in seconds, not the old one. That was what the simp intervention was. “So a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.” We do not want that dull, depressed spirit; we sharpen the countenance of our friends. We are here to sharpen one another in these scriptures so that we can go out and preach the gospel to our people, and we cannot do it if we are dull in spirit, depressed or distressed.

precepts.why:
“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” Go to the ants, thou sluggard; consider their ways and be wise. Unity is our strength and our wisdom. Alone you are weak; together we are strong.

“It is like the precious ointment upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, even Aaron’s beard: that went down to the skirts of his garments”. That ointment was only for Aaron, and this unity is only for the Israelites. “As the dew of Hermon, and as the dew that descended upon the mountains of Zion: for there the Lord commanded the blessing, even life for evermore.”

The unity of brethren is what the Most High finds good and pleasant, and that is how you come out of the depressed, weak spirit. It is the brethren together that sharpen one another as iron sharpens iron.

sense.text: “This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.” Some brothers are so depressed and so down on themselves that nothing but prayer and fasting will do. Some do not fast enough: they do not take the opportunity of the monthly fast, the bi-weekly fast, the Day of Atonement. These depressed, evil spirits cannot leave you except through prayer and fasting.

This is for the brothers who want to keep that wicked wife and her unclean children. “And if thy right eye offend thee”: that is your members, your family members, your friends. “Pluck it out, and cast it from thee”: separate yourself. You do not need them; you can start all over. You have the strength, the fortitude, and the brothers and the unity to do it; you cannot do it on your own.

“For it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell.” Sometimes we have to divorce ourselves from our friends and family for our own salvation. Their perspective is not what the Bible says: they will tell you it was not that bad and make you want to compromise. Do not take advice from people in the world, nor from those who are lukewarm in this truth. Do not look for itching ears that tell you what you want to hear; the scriptures tell you what you need to hear.

“Since thou wast precious in my sight”. The verse above shows he gave Egypt, Ethiopia and Seba, Somalia, for us: three nations of people for our salvation. That is how precious we are in the sight of the Most High. So stop, brothers, with the depressed spirit and the distressed spirit, and with giving in to your lust and lasciviousness, which only lead into a path of gross darkness.

“Thou hast been honourable”: we have been honorable, so do not be dishonorable. “And I have loved thee: therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” The Most High loved us so much that he gave nations, people, for our salvation.

“Fear not: for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west”. The Most High is letting us know we are precious in his sight. He is with us and he will gather us, so we have to see ourselves as such.
